basisClaims.statement: A clinically suspicious persistent palpable breast mass requires tissue diagnosis even when diagnostic mammography and targeted ultrasonography are negative.
basisClaims.limitation: Single current specialty guideline; biopsy technique depends on whether an imaging target exists and local specialist assessment.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with a persistently suspicious palpable breast mass despite negative mammography and targeted ultrasound.

basisClaims.statement: A small, asymptomatic, core-proven fibroadenoma that is radiologically and pathologically concordant and lacks atypia or concern for phyllodes tumor can be managed without routine excision.
basisClaims.limitation: This does not apply to discordance, atypia, phyllodes concern, symptoms, substantial growth, or a patient preference for removal.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with an asymptomatic concordant fibroadenoma proven by core biopsy.

basisClaims.statement: FHH commonly presents as lifelong, nonprogressive mild hypercalcemia with normal or mildly increased PTH, typically low urinary calcium excretion, and often a family history of hypercalcemia.
basisClaims.limitation: No individual feature is sufficient to distinguish FHH from primary hyperparathyroidism, and serum magnesium is not a reliable discriminator.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable patients undergoing outpatient evaluation of persistent PTH-dependent hypercalcemia.

basisClaims.statement: When FHH is suspected, urinary calcium excretion should be evaluated with a calcium-to-creatinine clearance ratio calculated from concurrent serum measurements and a 24-hour urine calcium and creatinine collection.
basisClaims.limitation: Collection quality, renal function, vitamin-D status, pregnancy, and thiazides can affect interpretation; the game does not treat the collection as localization imaging.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable patients with persistent hypercalcemia and nonsuppressed PTH when FHH and primary hyperparathyroidism are being differentiated.

basisClaims.statement: A calcium-to-creatinine clearance ratio below 0.01 supports suspicion for FHH but cannot confirm the diagnosis by itself because values overlap with primary hyperparathyroidism.
basisClaims.limitation: The exact 0.01 threshold is used only as a source-supported screening clue, not as a standalone diagnostic cutoff.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Patients with interpretable paired serum and 24-hour urine calcium and creatinine measurements.

basisClaims.statement: Suggestive biochemistry and family history should prompt family evaluation and genetic testing; a pathogenic FHH-associated variant can confirm the diagnosis, while negative testing does not exclude every clinically suspected case.
basisClaims.limitation: Variants of uncertain significance and mutation-negative clinically suspected FHH require specialist interpretation; the approved questions use a pathogenic CASR result when confirmation is stated.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Patients with a biochemical and family pattern that raises suspicion for FHH.

basisClaims.statement: Confirmed uncomplicated FHH is generally managed with reassurance and observation rather than parathyroid surgery, which usually does not correct the inherited calcium-sensing disorder.
basisClaims.limitation: Rare symptomatic or atypical FHH and coexisting primary hyperparathyroidism require specialist individualized management and are excluded from these variants.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic patients with confirmed FHH, stable mild hypercalcemia, and no authored complication or coexisting primary hyperparathyroidism.

basisClaims.statement: For an otherwise asymptomatic patient with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism, age under 50 years is an independent guideline criterion supporting parathyroidectomy.
basisClaims.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. Operative suitability, localization, genetic evaluation, and all other surgical criteria remain outside this focused pathway.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults younger than 50 years with confirmed asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism and no other operative criterion described in this pathway.

basisClaims.statement: For an adult with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism, skeletal assessment includes DXA at the lumbar spine, hip, and distal one-third radius.
basisClaims.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. This claim does not assign a universal DXA diagnostic threshold or determine surgery by bone density alone.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism undergoing standard skeletal assessment.

basisClaims.statement: In the scoped stable outpatient evaluation, repeat serum calcium together with intact PTH establishes the biochemical pattern of primary hyperparathyroidism before localization planning.
basisClaims.limitation: This single-source claim does not define every cause of hypercalcemia or make localization imaging diagnostic.
basisClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with prior hypercalcemia whose renal, vitamin-D, medication, and inherited-mimic context has already been reviewed.

items.reason: The existing diagnostic claim covers HIV/HCV evaluation in compatible isolated thrombocytopenia. It does not establish the new multilineage marrow-versus-flow-versus-sequencing ranking. The separate splenectomy calendar claim has an unresolved bibliographic identity. Neither can support the round-two key.
items.supportedAlternativeConsidered: Considered re-aiming to initial HIV/HCV evaluation. That duplicates the unchanged diagnostic siblings and does not adjudicate the owner's recollected marrow sequence or support a harder marrow decision. A negative viral result cannot supply the missing marrow indication.

items.reason: The ledger directly supports advance trigger-free planning in an MH-prepared facility for credibly documented susceptibility. It does not verify the named drug regimen, negative-panel/prior-exposure interpretation, exact capabilities, contracture-testing sequence or prophylactic dantrolene comparison that selects the round-two key.
items.supportedAlternativeConsidered: Considered testing only trigger-free planning versus routine anesthesia. That returns to the owner-rejected easy contrast and cannot provide specific close, defensible competing plans without verified agent/preparation facts. Treating a worksheet as proof of readiness would manufacture the missing evidence.

items.reason: The ledger supports pregnancy testing, the limited meaning of an early negative home test, and prompt specialist-capable assessment for symptomatic pregnancy. It does not verify the falling-hCG interpretation or exact transvaginal-versus-appendiceal-imaging-versus-aspiration priority used in round two.
items.supportedAlternativeConsidered: Considered re-aiming to immediate specialist assessment using the recorded disposition claim. Without a verified trajectory/diagnostic discriminator this is the same easy safety-recognition item the reviewer identified; using delayed care as the competitor would violate the brief. No supported PGY-2/3 replacement has been established.

items.reason: The recorded three-site baseline claim supports lumbar spine, hip and distal one-third radius in confirmed PHPT. It does not directly verify the hardware-side and radial-region comparative protocol used as the round-two key.
items.supportedAlternativeConsidered: Applied the reviewer's unscored-context suggestion in the separately versioned G05 candidate. Baseline DXA has already occurred and referral preceded it; no hardware choice, acquisition gate or technical-radius matrix is scored. This does not create a new accepted basic item.

items.reason: The recorded PTLD claims require tissue pathology rather than EBV DNA/imaging to establish and classify disease. They do not choose excision over core or verify fresh/fixed allocation, whole-specimen formalin handling or a cause for failed flow viability.

That repeats the easy evidence-gap recognition already rejected and does not satisfy the owner's request for close specific actions. Ranking targets, biopsy methods or processing would again require an unsupported deciding fact.
